rewrites.53A05736: The report keeps the series apart under three rules. rewrites.596D44CD: **Rio de Janeiro, Santa Marta and Rocinha.** The Rio Top Tour's first phase cost about R$230,000 (R$184,000 federal, R$46,000 state). The Cantagalo elevator cost about R$89 million and the Providência cable car R$75 million in a R$163 million package. Almost 10,000 officers were deployed at peak. The tours drew about 4,500 visitors in their first month in 2010. About 20 resident guides were working by 2015. In 2014, 81% of foreign visitors spent up to R$10 in Rocinha. The cable car stood idle for eight years and security collapsed in 2017, yet Rocinha drew 544,000 visitors in 2023. Access and safety were preconditions, not product. Resident guides continued after the programme that launched them.[^479]
rewrites.105ACAF2: **Soweto, Vilakazi Street.** The Hector Pieterson Museum cost R23.2 million, the Mandela House restoration about R9 million from corporate donors and Orlando Stadium about R280 million; the public-realm cost is not disclosed. The street drew about 1,000 tourists a day by January 2010. Sakhumzi grew from four employees in 2001 to about 110 in 2019. The ten restaurants provide more than 800 jobs, though the Mandela House company was liquidated. Upgrades amplified existing assets but benefits concentrated on street-front owners, so design governance and a resident precinct entity belong at the outset.[^481]
rewrites.06286A8D: **Costa Rica, ACTUAR.** UNDP GEF small grants funded the network from the 1990s. Law 8724 (2009) gave ICT duties without a budget. No state funding for the selling network has been identified. ACTUAR, founded in 2001, turned over more than USD 800,000 in 2013 for more than 30 member communities and dissolved at the end of 2018; its benefits stopped at association members. A management entity with its own selling channel was the engine and it did not survive donor exit.[^482]
rewrites.578C6562: **Soweto, Kliptown.** Kliptown received R436 million in its first allocation. The JDA spent about R497 million from 2001 to 2010 plus R40 million to 2013, Walter Sisulu Square cost R160 million to R180 million and a 48-room hotel R24 million. The business case projected almost 200,000 international visitors a year, but the museum drew about 4,000 a year by 2017 and the hotel traded above break-even only during the 2010 FIFA World Cup. Local small businesses took 5% of construction contract value. The site was looted in 2021. Heritage converts to local income only when operator, trader and guide product, security and services are funded before the ribbon is cut.[^483]
rewrites.48E8E662: Structured sessions were held with key stakeholders, extracted insights, mapped each to the study's framework of goals and objectives and aggregated them. rewrites.5B59BD26: Two gaps in the record matter: phase 1 engaged no airline, online travel agent or tour operator; the six demand-side engagements were proposed for phase 2. The Cape Town Air Access pipeline gives that test its agenda. As reported in November 2025, it targets routes from Africa, Saudi Arabia, Asia and Australia and has engaged Cathay Pacific, China Southern, Air India and IndiGo. The demand work drew instead on discussions with more than 20 stakeholders of its own. The outcomes of engagement phases 2 to 4 sit in no document in hand.[^487]
